about: ArtifactData batch for https://claude.ai/artifact/UcN4Lpz8yMHSyDCK69DmYM, collection playtests: the two Claude-played runs. A person pushes this after review; nothing here writes to the artifact. © 2026 justaskjoe. All rights reserved.

runs.contra: Rep climbed from 60 to the max of 100 while my star rating slid from 4.25 to 3.69, with reviews like 'Overpriced and pushy' (I never touched a tag), 'Case is always stocked' (my case held one 10c card) and 'Pulled a hit from their repack!' (I never made a repack). A booster box shows as worth ~250c, but it can't go on the rack, so opening it into packs (~170c) is the only way to sell it. On Card Night with zero packs, DJ Vee said 'the crowd still bought some packs'.
runs.confused: The star rating. It dropped on days that felt great and nothing told me why. And tells: most customers showed one and almost none were crooks, so by day 3 I ignored them. Prices also swing overnight: the 180c card I bought on day 1 was 'worth' 203c, not 251c, the next morning because Shellstorm demand dipped.
runs.best: Day 3: a 'perfect' card I paid 7c for looked like 208c and passed my UV lamp and loupe. DJ Vee's hint about perfect-looking promos made me buy the Spectrometer, re-scan it, and it was a fake. That's the game teaching me something. Also day 2: a browser paid 135c off the rack for the 60c blister I'd ordered the night before.
runs.worst: Days 5 and 6: my singles side was dead (everything I owned was 1-10c) and the day was just pack buyers and 'Your loss!' sellers. And day 6: the first estate lot was a vintage pack at 944c when I had 94c. Vintage was never reachable in my whole run.
runs.change: Explain the star rating every morning (which three things moved it and by how much) and make reviews match what actually happened in my shop. Make tells mean more: fewer of them on honest customers.
runs.bugs: Reviews mention things I never had (repacks, a vintage box on display). DJ Vee's day-8 close repeats the day-4 line 'Wave 3 reprint list is out' on the eve of Wave 4. Card Night with no packs still says the crowd bought packs.

runs.contra: Skrimp the scalper pays 31c a pack, more than my own customers (~28c). I sold him every pack three times (days 3, 5 and 9) for ~1,300c, by far my best income. Rep fell 73 to 43, but the star rating barely moved and nothing else got worse, so the 'bad' choice is the best one. The board flags Sticky in a hat, but watching catches them the same way, so refusing only loses the bounty.
runs.confused: Sealed supply. A Hive premium box I paid 230c for was 'worth' 216c the next morning because of a reprint nobody warned me about. A Shellstorm order was refused for 'allocation' when the gossip had named a Hive set. The rack only holds 16 packs, so 'no room' kept stopping me. Also the first loupe on a card cut its estimate from ~498c to ~280c.
runs.best: Day 1: a 'whole binder page for 14c' had a ~498c card in it (280c after the loupe), and Mimbo paid 258c for another card the same day. Day 8: Vault paid 762c for a Lopu Fox that had sat unnoticed in my back binder.
runs.worst: Days 4 and 6: 26 packs in stock and I sold about one pack each day. After the scalper days the shop just idled. And vintage: I bought the scale and the riser, the first lot was 1064c when I had 700c ('the estate can't go that low'), and the next one was 2675c.
runs.change: Make the scalper's cost visible and real (fewer buyers tomorrow, a rating hit, a 'Limit 2' reminder at the counter) or cap him. Bring estate vintage earlier and cheaper, or let me put a deposit down, so the vintage fixtures I buy can pay off.
runs.bugs: Reviews say 'Pulled a hit from their repack!' and 'Saw a vintage box on display' and I had neither. The day-8 close says 'Wave 3 reprint list is out' on the eve of Wave 4.
